answer.rationale: The degradation is confined to the primary region while settlement writes are at daily peak, which matches the regional-failover pattern in memory_b2 (fast latency recovery, clean traffic shift, errors recovered in minutes). A rollback (memory_b1) is plausible given the release 2 hours ago, but it is a slower, write-path-risky action during peak settlement and the regional confinement points away from a bad global build. Failover is the single intervention most likely to restore availability quickly without losing customer writes; I flag residual risk that the new release is the true cause, in which case failover may not fully resolve the p99 climb and rollback becomes the next-window action. I verify memory_b2 to confirm the failover record before committing.
